Delivered to `/tmp/opensip-design-corrections/v20-stage-proposal-review.v1/`: `assessment.json`, `assessment.md`, `probes.py`, `probe-results.json`, and a corrected two-file `overlay/`. Frozen19 and the proposal work tree are byte-unchanged.

**Custody.** Both before-hashes match frozen19; both after-hashes match the proposal work tree; exactly two files present. `parentManifestSha256` is unverified — `candidate-subject.v19/` holds only `docs/` and I could not locate the artifact it names.

**Verdict.** I agree with all four choices as design. I withhold assent from the proposal's exact schema bytes for one blocking defect.

**RC-1 (blocking).** `"$ref": "#/$defs/Ref/properties/domain"` is the first deep JSON pointer in the document — all 39 pre-existing refs are flat `#/$defs/<Name>`, and three resolvers resolve refs as `ref.split('/')[-1]` into `$defs`. `identity-model.py:589` (`deref`, called by the admission walk at every node) raises `KeyError: 'domain'`, so **core admission crashes** on any non-empty `outputDomains`; `check-identity.py:887` crashes the identity suite the same way. Reproduced by transcribing both functions verbatim (no frozen-tree imports). Two sharp consequences: it's an uncaught `KeyError`, not an `AdmissionError`; and `outputDomains: []` is the only value that still admits, because `walk` doesn't descend into an empty list — choice 3 survives by accident. In the suite, `rejects()` catches `KeyError`, so the domain-join negative would pass for the wrong reason while the positive aborts. Fix supplied and verified: flat `$defs/Domain`, both `items` pointing at it, `Ref.properties.domain` bytes untouched (check-identity.py:1367 reads that `['enum']` directly).

**Choices.** (1) Accept the design — this is real enforcement, not annotation: `['View']` and `['my-provider/output']` are admitted by frozen19 and refused by the proposal and my overlay; typed boundary live at `identity-model.py:685`, equality check unchanged at `:1407`, no new refusal name. (2) Accept — ownership is now total and invents nothing; one closable ambiguity remains, distinctness *within* one interface, whose concrete consequence is a cache-key collision (`stageSpecDigest` covers operation+parameters+outputSchema and feeds `cache-key`); RC-2 states it in eight lines. (3) Accept — no existing obligation contradicted, no `minItems`, and I decline to add one. (4) Accept — root's exact-15 coverage **verified by measurement**, and every binding re-verified against the model independently; RC-4 corrects the import strings, which invert the actual law at `:1428`.

Qualifications recorded as asked: nothing re-mints from *this* edit (the bundle isn't a digested artifact), but registered artifact documents do re-mint with no recipe change; no new public route (zero code, wider inputs to a pre-existing `ValidationError` class); no C2 vocabulary imported.

Honest limits: I did not run `close_run()` end-to-end — RC-1 is proven at the function admission calls, with the call path established by reading `identity-model.py:685-692` and `:1404`, not by executing it. I did not read all 108,707 bytes of contract prose line-by-line. The `$defs/Domain` duplicate needs a one-line pinning law in the checker owner's file, which I flagged as a merge obligation rather than delivering in a third file.
